report.headline: Projected for a modest usage increase in the EuroLeague, but the accompanying efficiency projection carries no real information.

projection.text: Usage rate is projected at 24.5% in the EuroLeague, up from 21.2% in the source NBA season, and above the target league's average of 20.3% (sd 4.2%); the 80% interval runs 20.4%-28.7%.

risks.text: True shooting percentage in the source season was 50.4%, or -0.73 standard deviations below the NBA average, marking scoring efficiency as a source-season weakness.

The true-shooting projection model loses to the trivial league-average baseline (4.7% MAE for both), meaning the 55.9% true-shooting projection is not more reliable than simply assuming league average and should not be used as a genuine forecast.
At the 95% level the intervals widen further, 18.2%-30.9% for usage and 45.2%-66.5% for true shooting, underscoring how imprecise the individual-level projections are.

Historically, players who made this NBA->EuroLeague move sat on average -0.31 standard deviations below their own league's average at the time of the move, a cohort profile that does not clearly match this subject's mixed indicators (above-average usage standing but below-average shooting efficiency).

strengths.text: Averaged 7.377 assists and a 33.3% assist rate per 75 possessions in the source season, indicating a heavy playmaking role.

The model's usage-rate projection beats a trivial league-average baseline (3.3% MAE vs 4.3%), and the fitted slope of 0.986 shows nearly full carry-over of standing, giving the 24.5% usage projection real weight.
Usage rate stood at +0.23 standard deviations above the NBA average in the source season, a modestly above-average role that the model projects to expand further in the EuroLeague.

uncertainty.text: The 80% interval for usage rate spans 8.3 percentage points-about two standard deviations of the EuroLeague's usage spread-so the model can rank this transition but not price it precisely; the true-shooting projection of 55.9% is worse than a simple league-average baseline (4.7% MAE vs 4.7%) and should not be treated as informative.
